0.content: A violet-glowing sword said to cut through mist and night fog, bestowed by the Shogun on her Hatamoto. It was shattered into a thousand pieces and later reforged from the fragments so that the weapon would inherit the Mistsplitter name; its hamon resembles flowing clouds. Takamine's sword broke in the Abyss, and the text says Mistsplitter had no successors and now lives only in stories, artworks and fairytales.

1.comment: Takamine the Mistsplitter: Takamine's wager with Asase Hibiki
1.content: Before leaving for the Abyss Takamine left Thundering Pulse with Hibiki and bet he would return alive and claim "the future" along with the bow; if he lost, she kept it. He did not return in time, so she won the bow. When what came back from the Abyss reached her she was no longer young and, in Shaft of Remembrance's telling, shot it to save him and kept their promise as her own.

2.comment: Takamine the Mistsplitter: Takamine in the children's rhyme
2.content: Inazuman children who love martial arts list the famous warriors as Arataki of the Front Gate, Iwakura the Successor, Kitain the Serpent and Takamine the Mistsplitter. The rhyme appears in Mistsplitter Reforged's description.
